newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Dying sea prompts Uzbek farmer to circle globe.
newsitem.headline: Dying sea prompts Uzbek farmer to circle globe.

text.p: An Uzbek farmer plans to travel around the world in a horse-drawn cart to bring attention to the former Soviet republic's dying Aral Sea, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.

"Our voyage around the world is not Don Quixotism," said the farmer, Mr. Utambekov, whose first name was not given. "The main goal is to attract the attention of those living in these countries to the environmental disaster in the Aral Sea."
The voyage will start in Nukus, a regional Uzbek capital, and take Utambekov across 18 countries.
To boost production in Central Asia in the 1960s, the Soviet leadership diverted the waters of two large rivers feeding the Aral Sea to irrigate cotton fields.
The results were catastrophic. The volume of the inland sea, once the world's fourth largest lake, has dropped by three quarters.
A once busy fishing industry has all but disappeared and nearby settlements, rife with respiratory and other diseases, have turned into ghost towns.
